paper.title_en: Geometric Control of Electronic Decoherence in a Chiral Spin-Orbit Coupled Helix
paper.abstract_en: While chirality is known to impact chemical and optical properties of molecular systems, as well as their biological function, far less is known about its impact on quantum coherence. By considering a chiral helix as a paradigmatic model, we show that within the Born-Markov regime, changing the degree of helical twist can be used to modulate the electronic decoherence rate. Moderate to strong spin-orbit coupling between next-nearest-neighbor sites along the helix are shown to give rise to a strong dependence of the electronic decoherence rate on the degree of chirality. The effect of chirality on electronic decoherence rates is also seen to be strongly impacted by the spatial and temporal correlations between the local environmental fluctuations to which the local excitations along the helix are subject. Our results show that chirality can serve as a tunable design parameter for quantum engineering and highlight the importance role environmental correlations can play in determining how chirality affects electronic decoherence rates.
